\subsubsection{Measuring this block on chip}

The converter is characterised end to end with no analog pad measurement ---
and its gain has never been checked in system.
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
\item Gain and intercept: set \texttt{AFE\_ADCSRCSEL}~=~4, drive an external
  ramp onto \texttt{atb\_d} (\texttt{AFE\_DBGDIREN}~=~1,
  \texttt{AFE\_DBGBUFEN}~=~0), fit slope and intercept per die. The
  \(1.535\times\) slope, \SI{0.441}{\volt} intercept and
  \SI{1.591}{\milli\volt} effective LSB of Table~\ref{tab:adc-transfer} hold
  to \SI{0.10}{\percent} across process corners in simulation; their
  die-to-die spread is neither measured nor simulable
  (Section~\ref{sss:adc-mc}), which is what makes this step per-die rather
  than per-lot.
\item Zero code: set \texttt{AFE\_ADCSRCSEL}~=~1 and average the common-mode
  rail. That code is the origin of the current axis and carries the
  converter's offset and the common-mode value together --- the combination a
  current reading needs.
\item Dither before averaging: with the electrode isolated the amplifier
  output noise is tens of microvolts, below one code, so step the common-mode
  DAC over three of its \SI{529}{\micro\volt} codes (together they span one
  converter code); only then does averaging reach the quantisation floor.
\item Observe the sampling node itself at per-channel slot 9 between
  conversions only.
\end{enumerate}
This test fabric is design intent; it is not yet in the schematics.
